title: Chapter 10 Quiz: Final Project & Course Review
description: Test your cumulative knowledge of Spring Boot, including the final project concepts and all previous chapters.

questions.question: Which annotation combines @Configuration, @EnableAutoConfiguration, and @ComponentScan?
questions.explanation: @SpringBootApplication is the convenience annotation that includes all three.

questions.question: In Spring Security, @PreAuthorize can be used on service methods, not just controllers.
questions.explanation: Method security works on any Spring bean method, including services.

questions.question: The annotation used to inject a mock into a Spring Boot test is _________.
questions.explanation: @MockBean is used in tests that load a Spring context; @Mock is for pure unit tests.

questions.question: Which HTTP method is idempotent and safe?
questions.explanation: GET is both safe (no side effects) and idempotent (repeated requests have same effect).

questions.question: When using JPA, the `@OneToMany` relationship defaults to eager fetching.
questions.explanation: @OneToMany defaults to LAZY fetching; @ManyToOne defaults to EAGER.

questions.question: The Spring Boot Actuator endpoint that provides JVM metrics is _________.
questions.explanation: The /metrics endpoint exposes runtime metrics including memory, threads, and garbage collection.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a valid `ddl-auto` option for JPA?
questions.explanation: Valid values are none, validate, update, create, create-drop; 'automatic' is not a standard option.

questions.question: A microservice should always share a single database with other services.
questions.explanation: Microservices aim for decentralized data; each service typically owns its own database.

questions.question: To enable method security with @PreAuthorize, you need to add _________ to a configuration class.
questions.explanation: You must add @EnableGlobalMethodSecurity(prePostEnabled = true) to enable @PreAuthorize.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the `@RequestParam` annotation?
questions.explanation: @RequestParam binds query parameters from the URL (e.g., ?name=John).

questions.question: Spring Boot automatically secures Actuator endpoints when Spring Security is added.
questions.explanation: Actuator endpoints are not automatically secured; you must configure security rules.

questions.question: The default port for the Eureka server dashboard is _________.
questions.explanation: Eureka server typically runs on port 8761.

questions.question: Which annotation would you use to handle a global exception across all controllers?
questions.explanation: Both @ControllerAdvice and @RestControllerAdvice can be used for global exception handling.

questions.question: In JPA, the `cascade = CascadeType.ALL` on a @OneToMany relationship means that when you delete the parent, all children will be deleted.
questions.explanation: CascadeType.ALL includes REMOVE, so deletion cascades to child entities.

questions.question: The annotation used to mark a class as a REST controller is _________.
questions.explanation: @RestController combines @Controller and @ResponseBody, suitable for REST APIs.

questions.question: Which of the following is a synchronous inter‑service communication style?
questions.explanation: HTTP/REST is synchronous; message queues and event streams are asynchronous.

questions.question: Spring Cloud Gateway is built on the reactive stack (WebFlux).
questions.explanation: Spring Cloud Gateway is reactive and uses Netty as the underlying server.

questions.question: In a Spring Boot test, the _________ annotation is used to start a full application context with a random port.
questions.explanation: @SpringBootTest with webEnvironment = RANDOM_PORT starts the embedded server on a random port.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the `@Valid` annotation in a controller?
options: To validate the request body before method execution
questions.explanation: `@Valid` triggers validation on the annotated parameter (e.g., @RequestBody).

questions.question: In Spring Security, `.anyRequest().authenticated()` must be placed after more specific rules.
questions.explanation: Rules are evaluated in order; the catch‑all should come last.
